Subject: Activation checkpoints & scaling charter for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Lucas —

Following our kickoff, I wanted to put a lightweight activation checklist and scaling charter on the table so we can align expectations before we provision the Dedicated GPU pool. High-level asks from our side: region, baseline vs burst QPS (or RPS), expected peak window(s), and any compliance gating (KMS/HSM, audit log retention).

Proposed activation checkpoints (rough):
- Checkpoint 1 (Week 0): Provision 8x A100-equivalent GPUs in us-east-1, network config, KMS key escrow test
- Checkpoint 2 (Week 1): Canary traffic (5% -> 25% over 48h), KV cache priming and latency histogram baseline
- Checkpoint 3 (Week 2): Scale test to expected peak for 2h, autoscaling policy tuning and burst token verification
- Checkpoint 4 (Week 3): SLA handover, runbook, and 24/7 on-call handoff

Autoscaling / burst model questions:
- Do you want strict SLOs for tail latency (p95/p99) or an economical policy that allows short tail spikes to hit burst capacity?
- Any preference for regional primary (us-east-1/us-west-2) vs multi-region active/standby?

If you can confirm the region and expected baseline/peak numbers I’ll have Marissa map a concrete GPU pool config and Rishi draft the autoscaling policy. I’ve attached a short one-pager we’ll iterate on.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks for the clear checklist. A few quick answers:

- Region: primary us-east-1, secondary can be us-west-2 for DR (we prefer single-region active initially)
- Baseline: ~120 reqs/min (steady daytime), Peak: up to 900 reqs/min during batch windows (approx 30m bursts, 3x per day)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 600ms for our user-facing gen endpoints; internal batch work can accept higher latency
- Compliance: we need KMS integration for key management and 365-day audit log retention; legal will request a short attestation for data residency

We also have a procurement milestone: budget approval is expected this week but DocuSign routing will be next Monday. Ops will need a test window for an end-to-end run.

Thanks Lucas — got the numbers. Based on the profile above I sketched an initial capacity and policy:

- Initial pool: 8x H100-similar GPUs (reserved), with room to expand to 16 within 72 hours
- Autoscaling: target CPU/GPU util 60-75% with continuous batching; scale-up threshold at sustained 75% for 3m, scale-down after 10m of sustained <50%
- Burst policy: token bucket allowing up to 3x baseline for 30m, capped by a safety limit that triggers fallback to a lower-cost model variant if sustained >45m
- Canary plan: 5% -> 15% -> 35% -> 100% over 72 hours with health checks (p95/p99, error-rate, token-consumption)

I added a couple of operational notes in the Drive doc (link below): we should pre-warm KV cache for the most common prompts to avoid cold-start p99 spikes. Also recommending a manual SLA exception during first 2 weeks so we can perform live tuning.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-stargazer-activation

If that looks good I’ll produce the capacity estimate and an initial runbook (playbook for run-of-show).

Subject: Re: Activation checkpoints & scaling charter for Dedicated GPU pool — capacity test results

Ran the 2-hour peak sim today. TL;DR: baseline config holds; burst tokens sufficient for two 30m bursts back-to-back but p99 jumps when KV cache cold. Notes attached.

Highlights:
- Test sim: ramped to 900 reqs/min over 10m, held for 2h, then 50% downshift
- p95: 180–210ms; p99: 520–760ms (cold-cache spikes up to 900ms)
- GPU util: avg 68% during steady, peaked 88% in the first 12m of each burst
- Network: no packet-loss observed; pinned kernel version is ideal for H100 path

Recommendations:
- Increase pre-warm TTL for KV cache and run a 24h priming job before full activation
- Start canary at 7% with 24h dwell and 10% increments thereafter (safer given cold-cache p99 behavior)
- Provision an extra 2 GPUs as warm standby for first 72h to absorb cold-cache-induced spikes

Attachment: capacity-estimate-stargazer.xlsx

—Jonas
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
